sections.h2: Who handles your Albany tax bill
sections.html:
Albany splits the work between two city offices. The Treasurer takes in payments and the Assessor decides the value behind the bill. You will find the Treasurer at 24 Eagle Street in City Hall, 518-434-5036. The Assessor works upstairs in Room 302, reachable at 518-434-5155. The City Charter names the Treasurer chief fiscal officer, responsible for collecting every city tax and any other money the city is owed.

  • Treasurer: bills, payments, receipts, changes of address, returned payments
  • Assessor: values, STAR and other exemption forms, grievance forms, parcel maps
  • Board of Assessment Review: hears complaints about assessments, with members appointed by the Common Council to five-year terms

Pay the whole bill, or the first half, by January 31. Seniors who qualify get until February 6. If a deadline lands on a weekend it slides to the next business day, and since January 31 falls on a Sunday in 2027, the working deadline that year is Monday, February 1.

All owners may now pay in halves. The first half is due at the deadline. The second is billed in early July and may be paid any time after the first, plus interest. The online system accepts full payments only, so a split payment has to go by check or cash.

Bills are meant to arrive by January 12. Missing yours? Print a copy from the Treasurer's online lookup. Penalties for late payment are mandatory under state law, and the city has no power to waive the interest. A returned payment costs $34.

This $180 per unit charge sits on the tax bill itself. Until 2026 it came as its own mailing. When a prior year's fee goes unpaid (it was $90 per unit for 2025), the balance moves onto the next tax bill with late charges added. If you think the fee should not apply to your property, email the Treasurer or call 518-434-5036 and ask for an exemption application. Owners the city already knew were exempt in 2023 and 2024 were not billed in 2025.

For a seller the point is simple: an old unpaid fee is part of what you owe at closing. Ask the Treasurer for a payoff that includes it, then check that total against the January bill in your hands.

Mail, the website and City Hall all work. Skip bill-payment services if you can. Their envelopes tend to carry no postmark, and Albany counts the USPS postmark only, never a postage meter stamp.

Payment methodDetails
MailCheck payable to City of Albany, sent to City Treasurer, Room 109, City Hall, Albany, NY 12207. Include the bill number, your signature, the date and any interest owed.
Online, e-checkCosts 50 cents. Online payments can take up to five business days to show.
Online, credit card25 cents plus 1.95 percent of the payment
In personRoom 110 at City Hall, weekdays from 8:30 a.m., with later hours from January 29 to 31

A self-addressed stamped envelope gets you a receipt immediately. Without one, receipts are mailed in bulk in late March or April. Online receipts post within 48 hours.

The window opens May 1 and closes on Grievance Day, the fourth Tuesday in May. Pick up the form at the Assessor's office once May 1 arrives and return it by that Tuesday. Complaints go before the Board of Assessment Review under Chapter 42 of the Albany General Code.

Assessments move when buildings are built, burned or torn down, and when the city refreshes the whole roll to keep it even. Parcel maps are available to view at the Assessor's office. The board weighs market value and ignores how heavy the bill feels, so show it a recent sale of a comparable house nearby, a repair estimate or an appraisal.

Apply for exemptions at the Assessor's office between January 1 and March 1. Basic STAR is meant for owners who live in the house. All owners sign the form and attach a photocopy of a driver's license showing residence. For Enhanced STAR help, call 518-434-5155.

New York's Tax Department pays STAR as a credit. You register once, the payment arrives ahead of school tax, and it continues yearly as long as you stay eligible. On a sale, end your registration. The buyer signs up after the house becomes a primary residence.

At closing, any open balance comes out of your proceeds and the current year is divided between you and the buyer on the closing statement. No check is needed at the table, but the figure has to be exact, so get it from the Treasurer, at 518-434-5036 on weekdays, before the closing date.

  • Request the current balance, including any waste fee carried over, and save the reply by email
  • If the first half is paid and the July half has not been billed yet, the buyer typically gets a credit for the months you owned
  • Confirm with the Assessor that your exemption ends or moves in line with the new owner's status

A cash buyer can take over the same payoff and still close fast. Owing the city does not end a sale; it changes only what is left for you once the statement is settled. Gather the parcel number, your last bill and your mailing address before calling so the answer comes back the same day.

Sellers get better results when the paperwork is lined up before a buyer appears. Start with the tax side, because it is the part that cannot be guessed.

  1. Print your current bill from the online lookup and note whether it is paid in full or by installment.
  2. Check the bill for the waste collection fee, including any amount left over from last year.
  3. Ask the Assessor whether any exemption is on the parcel and how it should be handled at transfer.
  4. Write down who will answer questions for you at the closing, and give that person the Treasurer's number.

These steps take little time and head off the usual delay, a payoff figure that arrives late or differs from the closing statement.

Albany has about 101,698 residents, and owners occupy about 38.2 percent of homes. The median value of an owner-occupied home is $234,700. Much of the older housing near the river is row houses, with roofs, porches and boilers a buyer will want inspected. With so many rentals, plenty of sellers own small multifamily buildings and should confirm each unit's waste fee before requesting a payoff.

faqs.q: What is the Albany property tax deadline?
faqs.a: January 31, or February 6 for eligible seniors. A weekend deadline moves to the next business day, which makes it February 1 in 2027. Mailed payments are judged by USPS postmark.

faqs.q: Can I split my Albany tax bill into two payments?
faqs.a: Yes. Half is due at the January deadline and the rest after the July bill, with interest added. Only checks or cash work for installments, not the online system.

faqs.q: Where do I get a copy of my Albany tax bill or receipt?
faqs.a: Use the Treasurer's online lookup or email the Treasurer's billing address. Mailed receipts go out in bulk in late March or April, and online receipts show up within 48 hours.
The fourth Tuesday in May. Forms are at the Assessor's office, City Hall Room 302, from May 1, and the complaint has to be filed by that day.

faqs.q: Do I owe Albany tax if I sell mid-year?
faqs.a: Only for the months you owned. The closing statement divides the year, and any unpaid balance goes to the Treasurer out of your proceeds, so ask for the payoff before closing.
